boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along Amherst corridors near UMass Amherst, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Amity Street: Amherst Cinema Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Amity Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the film schedule, then use the cinema’s directions page to orient yourself at the Amity and Pleasant streets intersection.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit cinema at the downtown Amity Street crossroads.
cards.evidence_claim: Amherst Cinema Arts Center is at 28 Amity Street, at the intersection of Amity Street and North and South Pleasant streets.
cards.access_notes: Screenings require checking the current schedule and ticket availability.

cards.title: Amity Street: Gallery A3
cards.subtitle: Amity Street corridor
cards.notes: Look for the gallery suite at 28 Amity Street and check its current exhibition information before making a dedicated visit.
cards.short_summary: A named visual-art stop in the same downtown building as the cinema.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Amherst’s downtown art-walking-tour map lists Gallery A3 at 28 Amity Street, suite 1D.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current exhibition hours with Gallery A3 before visiting.

cards.title: Amity Street: Amherst History Museum
cards.subtitle: Amity Street corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Simeon Strong House to view exhibits and artifacts interpreted by the Amherst Historical Society; check program details first.
cards.short_summary: The town history museum occupies the 1750-era Simeon Strong House.
cards.evidence_claim: The Amherst Historical Society governs the Amherst History Museum in the 1750-era Simeon Strong House at 67 Amity Street.
cards.access_notes: Review the museum’s current exhibitions and opening information before travel.

cards.title: South Pleasant Street: Mead Art Museum
cards.subtitle: South Pleasant Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk onto the Amherst College quadrangle for the museum, then use its current program information to choose an exhibition or event.
cards.short_summary: An Amherst College art museum on the quadrangle.
cards.evidence_claim: Amherst College identifies the Mead Art Museum at 41 Quadrangle Drive, reached from the South Pleasant Street campus corridor.
cards.access_notes: Check the Mead’s current gallery and event information before visiting.

cards.title: South Pleasant Street: Beneski Museum of Natural History
cards.subtitle: South Pleasant Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Amherst College’s museum information to plan a look at natural-history collections and confirm public visiting arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A natural-history museum associated with Amherst College.
cards.evidence_claim: Amherst College identifies the Beneski Museum of Natural History as one of the institutions visited by its students alongside other Amherst museums.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current visitor access and hours with the Beneski Museum.

cards.title: Main Street: Emily Dickinson Homestead
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the museum’s site material to connect the Homestead’s Main Street setting with the landscape and the Dickinson family grounds.
cards.short_summary: Emily Dickinson’s home stands on the Main Street museum grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: The Emily Dickinson Museum documents that the Homestead and Evergreens were on the Dickinson family’s Main Street grounds.
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s current tour, grounds, and ticket information before visiting.

cards.title: Main Street: The Evergreens
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Pair the Evergreens with the Homestead and follow the museum’s site interpretation for the two Dickinson family houses and grounds.
cards.short_summary: Austin and Susan Dickinson’s house is part of the Main Street museum site.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Amherst lists The Evergreens, the Austin Dickinson Home, on its National Register properties page.
cards.source_title: National Register of Historic Places | Amherst, MA
cards.access_notes: Visitor access is governed by the Emily Dickinson Museum; verify current arrangements.

cards.title: Boltwood Avenue: Amherst Town Common
cards.subtitle: Boltwood Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or chair for a scheduled public program; the town lists seasonal concerts on the Common with specific dates and times.
cards.short_summary: A civic green used for scheduled downtown music programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Amherst lists its Downtown Summer Concert Series at the Town Common on Boltwood Avenue and describes it as free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Downtown Summer Concert Series | Town of Amherst
cards.access_notes: Free access applies to the listed concert series; verify dates and weather plans for any event.

cards.title: Boltwood Walk: UMass Downtown
cards.subtitle: Boltwood Walk corridor
cards.notes: Check the town calendar for public UMass Downtown activities, including the Graduate School’s Summer Seminar Series, before heading downtown.
cards.short_summary: A UMass Amherst downtown venue used for public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Amherst calendar identifies UMass Downtown as the location for a public Summer Seminar Series with the UMass Amherst Graduate School.
cards.access_notes: Programs vary; consult the current calendar for event details and registration requirements.

cards.title: State Street: Puffer’s Pond
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the town’s pond page to plan a daylight nature visit for walking, birdwatching, fishing, canoeing, picnicking, or swimming.
cards.short_summary: A town-recognized recreation area with water and nature activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Amherst describes Puffer’s Pond as a recreational area for fishing, birdwatching, nature walks, canoeing, picnicking, and swimming.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted town guidance and conditions for water and recreation activities.
